key_insight: OpenFrontiers separates scientific rediscovery from solution retrieval, finding that LLM agents rarely solve recently resolved mathematics problems without external access.
engineering_relevance: Formally checked benchmarks with controlled retrieval conditions can help engineers distinguish genuine reasoning gains from access to published solutions.
method: Build a structured corpus of 12,151 open research problems across disciplines.
Create a 200-problem mathematics benchmark with reviewed Lean 4 statements and a quality-filtered HQ-50 subset.
Evaluate formal proofs using two independent checkers in an isolated sandbox under closed-book, frozen-retrieval, and live-web conditions.
evidence_signal: Seven LLM agents evaluated on HQ-50 under a standardized budget achieved at most 7 of 40 resolved problems closed-book; live-web success mostly reflected retrieval of published solutions.
watch_item: Results on a small, quality-filtered mathematics subset may not generalize to the broader cross-disciplinary corpus.
paper_title: OpenFrontiers: A Collection of Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Scientific Rediscovery
